title: Learning Responsibility-Attributed Adversarial Scenarios for Testing Autonomous Vehicles

control_signal.value: Designer-chosen careful-and-competent-driver reference model (FSM, CC-JP, RSS) defining attribution, plus online-selected adversary and closed-loop reward terms; no user-set behavior attribute.

control_mechanism.value: Gaussian-mixture diffusion adversary policy, fine-tuned by reinforcement learning (clipped-ratio policy gradient per denoising step) in closed loop with shaping rewards; attribution verified by counterfactual rollout where a reference driver replaces the target.

base_model.value: Gaussian-mixture diffusion model: ResNet-18 map encoder, temporal convolutional denoiser, 8 mixture components; gradient-boosting adversary selector with temporal confirmation gate.

datasets.value: nuScenes (training and primary evaluation); AD4CHE highway and rounD roundabout for cross-dataset transfer without retraining.

metrics.value: Responsibility validity (FSM, CC-JP, RSS attribution %), severity diversity Hcrit, positive braking-deficit exposure BD+%, infeasibility IP%.

controllability_evidence.value: CARS keeps 88.7% FSM attribution, about twice the strongest external baseline; SafeSim 44.8%, K=1 ablation 45.2%, IP% 0.04 for CARS.

stated_limitations.value: Reference models are longitudinal, so attribution is strongest for longitudinal conflicts; one active adversary at a time; only vehicles evaluated, no vulnerable road users.

notes: Adversarial testing focus; control is over attributability of collisions, not a user-specified style or attribute.
